function.name: search_documents
function.description: Search the Treasury Bulletin corpus and return the most relevant passages, each with its source document and YYYY-MM bulletin date.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. 'national defense expenditures 1940'.

top_k.description: How many passages to return (default 6; max 20).

function.name: grep_documents
function.description: Grep for an exact text pattern over the Treasury Bulletin files (like grep). The most reliable way to pin a row label/category/value. Returns 'file:line: text'. Substring (default, case-insensitive) or regex.

pattern.description: Text or regex, e.g. 'National defense' or '2,602'.

year.description: Optional 4-digit year filter (ignored if file_name set).

regex.description: If true, treat pattern as a regex (default false).

function.name: read_document
function.description: Read a slice of one Treasury Bulletin document by exact file name (financial tables are Markdown). Lines are numbered; page on by increasing start_line.

num_lines.description: How many lines to return (default 100; capped at 400).

function.name: list_documents
function.description: List available Treasury Bulletin documents, optionally filtered by 4-digit year.

year.description: Optional 4-digit year, e.g. '1940'. Empty lists all (capped).

function.name: compute
function.description: Execute Python (numpy/pandas available) for calculations and table analysis; returns stdout and the last expression's value. Use for ALL arithmetic over retrieved figures. Fresh sandbox each call.

function.name: submit_report
function.description: Finish the task: submit your final answer and the supporting path. This is the ONLY way to end -- do NOT print the report as text. Cite only observation ids (obs_N) that were actually delivered to you.

answer.description: Only the final value, in the units the question asks, or 'DATA NOT AVAILABLE'. No working or other figures: those belong in the path claims.

path.description: Supporting steps; [] only when answer is DATA NOT AVAILABLE.

claim.description: what that observation shows, or the calculation

depends_on.description: earlier step ids whose figures a compute step used
